claims.claimText: Mission 360: Inside BJP's Push for a Two-Thirds Majority and the Battle Over India's Constitutional Future

claims.claimText: After the shock defeat of the delimitation-cum-women's reservation bill on April 17, 2026, the BJP launched a high-stakes strategy to secure 360+ Lok Sabha seats — enough for a two-thirds majority — by engineering defections, targeting regional parties, and leveraging its historic Bengal win. The outcome will determine whether the government can reshape India's electoral map through constitutional reform.

claims.claimText: What is Mission 360?: Mission 360 is the BJP's strategy to secure a two-thirds majority (360+ seats) in the Lok Sabha, enabling it to pass constitutional amendments without opposition support. The strategy involves engineering defections from opposition parties and leveraging the NDA's recent electoral momentum after winning West Bengal.
claims.normalizedText: what mission 360 mission 360 bjps strategy secure twothirds majority 360 seats lok sabha enabling it pass constitutional amendments without opposition support strategy involves engineering defections from opposition parties and leveraging ndas recent electoral momentum after winning west bengal

claims.claimText: Why does the BJP need a two-thirds majority?: Constitutional amendments require a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in each House of Parliament. The BJP's legislative agenda — delimitation (redrawing constituencies), implementing women's reservation, One Nation One Election, and judicial reforms — all require constitutional amendments that cannot pass without opposition support.
claims.normalizedText: why does bjp need twothirds majority constitutional amendments require twothirds majority members present and voting each house parliament bjps legislative agenda delimitation redrawing constituencies implementing womens reservation one nation one election and judicial reforms all require constitutional amendments that cannot pass without opposition support

claims.claimText: What is delimitation and why is it controversial?: Delimitation is the redrawing of constituency boundaries based on population. The 1971 census freeze expires after 2026. Southern states oppose delimitation based on the 2011 census because their better population control would reduce their seat share relative to northern states. The government proposes increasing Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats to accommodate population growth without reducing absolute seats of any state.
claims.normalizedText: what delimitation and why it controversial delimitation redrawing constituency boundaries based population 1971 census freeze expires after 2026 southern states oppose delimitation based 2011 census because their better population control would reduce their seat share relative northern states government proposes increasing lok sabha from 543 850 seats accommodate population growth without reducing absolute seats any state

claims.claimText: How did the TMC MPs defect to the NDA?: Twenty Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MPs joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), a Tripura-based registered unrecognised party. This move bypasses anti-defection hurdles because a merger of two-thirds of a party's MPs with another party is legally valid. The NCPI then aligned with the NDA, effectively boosting the ruling coalition's strength by 20 seats.
claims.normalizedText: how did tmc mps defect nda twenty trinamool congress lok sabha mps joined nationalist citizens party india ncpi tripurabased registered unrecognised party this move bypasses antidefection hurdles because merger twothirds partys mps with another party legally valid ncpi then aligned with nda effectively boosting ruling coalitions strength by 20 seats

claims.claimText: What happens if the government reaches 360 seats?: If the NDA reaches a two-thirds majority, it could pass the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill to increase Lok Sabha to 850 seats based on the 2011 census, implement women's reservation from the 2029 elections, advance the One Nation One Election framework, and pursue judicial reforms including a unified pension code and appointment commission.
